claims.statement: The default Nextest filter excludes shared application tests from diagnostic binaries while retaining independent capture_send_tests in the workbench capture binary; app-server process fixtures run in a serialized group.
The login crate tests real callback parsing limits and private login-home cleanup, including filesystem identity drift.
Refresh endpoint tests exercise the fixed ordinary-build authority and, under the debug fixture feature, reject unsafe loopback endpoint forms.

The earlier component LEAK and original Project Work appearance-fade LEAK retain their limits; the separate native media follow-up records passing full-suite and repeated checks with recovered lock and firewall history, without a new controlled lock comparison or an explanation of the earlier LEAK.

Nextest serializes native-media exchanges and reserves global test threads for selected packet-flow, collaboration-disclosure and two short-frame composer/progress fixtures with their assertions retained; these rules do not establish display performance.

The native Project and nested Work follow-up retains its initial three full-suite failures and unexplained resume-test LEAK, ten isolated passes of the unchanged UI artifact, fixture correction and final 2921-pass workspace run as separate evidence rather than rewriting earlier failures.

The later lifecycle acceptance preserves two earlier leaky passes and clean isolated controls separately from its final 2924-pass, 1159-skipped workspace run with no LEAK; the earlier marker cause remains unknown.

The control follow-up retained its missing-binary setup failure and stale per-thread reviewer fixture failure separately. It explicitly sets global Automatic Review, preserves native permission and request-count assertions, and passes three native permission tests plus one database hold test; real UI and provider probes remain separate from the unrepeated full workspace suite.
